text: The guide had not exaggerated, which Farrukh found he minded rather more than if he had. The track ran on into country that had stopped bothering to be anything in particular - no wall, no tower, no pair of riders working the road in the bored, deliberate way the road out of Herat had still been worked a week ago. What there was instead were smaller things, and he noticed them for some while before he let himself decide what they meant. The cistern at the midday stop stood lower than a caravan would have left it, and the rope on its hook was still wet to the hand. Brush had been cut back from the shade side, low down, the cuts pale and green where the sap had not yet gone brown. A fire had been made in the lee of a stone and then put out with some care - not scattered the way a caravan scatters one on a cold morning, but pressed flat and covered over, the way a fire is put out by people who would rather it were not counted afterwards. And a little past the cistern the tracks left the track: several sets of them, one small, all going out across the broken ground where the walking was harder and the view of it from the road was harder still.
